_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 27 (Isaac's blessing; Jacob deceives). Saadia-specific moves: v.1 'לביך' = 'I am at your service' (consistent w/ B22:1); v.4,7,9,14,17,31 'אלואנא' = 'savory/colored dishes' (Saadia uses 'colored varieties' for מטעמים); v.28 'דסם' = 'fat/oil' (Saadia's term for משמני — the rich portion); v.40 'אד'א אסתולית פככת אצרה' = 'when you grow strong, you shall break his bond' (Saadia interprets תריד as gaining strength, not lamenting); v.41 'חקד' = 'harbored hatred' for ישטם.

translations.1: And when Isaac had grown old, his eyes had ceased from seeing; and he called Esau his elder son, and said to him: 'My son.' He said: 'I am at your service.'
translations.2: He said: 'Behold, I have grown old; I do not know the day of my death.
translations.3: Now take up your gear — your weapon and your bow — and go out to the wilderness, and hunt for me game.
translations.4: And prepare for me savory dishes as I love, and bring them to me, that I may eat — so that my soul may bless you before I die.'
translations.5: And Rebekah was listening when Isaac said this to Esau his son. And when Esau went to the wilderness to hunt game to bring it,
translations.6: Rebekah said to Jacob her son: 'Behold, I heard your father Isaac saying to Esau your brother,
translations.7: "Bring me game, and make me savory dishes; let me eat — that I may bless you before God before my death."
translations.8: Now, my son, accept from me what I command you concerning this:
translations.9: Go to the flock, and take for me from there two choice kids of the goats; and I shall make them as savory dishes for your father, as he loves.
translations.10: And you shall bring them to your father; let him eat — that he may bless you before his death.'
translations.11: Jacob said to her: 'Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man; and I am a smooth man.
translations.12: Perhaps my father shall feel me; and I shall be in his sight as a mocker; and I shall bring upon myself a curse, and not a blessing.'
translations.13: His mother said to him: 'Upon me is the warding off of your curse, my son; only accept from me, and go take it for me.'
translations.14: And he went, and took them, and brought them to his mother; and his mother made them savory dishes, as his father loved.
translations.15: And Rebekah took the choice garments of Esau her elder son, which were with her in the house; and she clothed Jacob her younger son.
translations.16: And the skins of the kids of the goats she put upon his hands, and upon the smoothness of his neck.
translations.17: And she set the savory dishes, and the bread which she had made, in the hand of Jacob her son.
translations.18: And he came in to his father, and said: 'O my father.' He said: 'I am at your service. Who are you, my son?'
translations.19: Jacob said to his father: 'I am Esau your firstborn; I have done as you commanded me. Arise now, sit, and eat of my game — so that your soul may bless me.'
translations.20: He said: 'How is it that you have hastened to find it, my son?' He said: 'For God your Lord caused [it] to come before me.'
translations.21: He said: 'Draw near, that I may feel you, my son — are you my son Esau, or not?'
translations.22: And he drew near to him; and he felt him. And he said: 'The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.'
translations.23: And he did not recognize him — for his hands were like the hands of Esau his brother, hairy. So he blessed him.
translations.24: And he said to him: 'Are you my son Esau?' He said: 'I am he.'
translations.25: He said: 'Bring it to me, that I may eat of my son's game, so that my soul may bless you.' And he brought it to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank.
translations.26: And Isaac his father said to him: 'Draw near and kiss me, my son.'
translations.27: And he drew near, and kissed him; and he smelled the smell of his garments, and blessed him. And he said: 'Behold the smell of my son — like the smell of a garden which God has blessed.
translations.28: May God give you of the dew of the sky, and of the fat of the earth, and abundance of grain and grape-juice.
translations.29: May the nations serve you, and the peoples bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. The one who curses you, may he be cursed; and the one who blesses you, may he be blessed.'
translations.30: And when Isaac had finished blessing Jacob — it was just as he had gone out from before him, that Esau his brother came in from his hunt.
translations.31: And he too made savory dishes, and brought them to his father; and he said: 'Let my father arise, and eat of his son's game — so that your soul may bless me.'
translations.32: And his father said to him: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.'
translations.33: And Isaac was struck with great alarm; and he said: 'Who then is the one who hunted game and brought it to me, and I ate of it before you came, and I blessed him? And he shall also be blessed.'
translations.34: When Esau heard his father's words, he cried out a great and very bitter cry; and he said to him: 'Bless me — me also, O my father!'
translations.35: He said: 'Your brother came with cunning, and took your blessing.'
translations.36: He said: 'Rightly was he named Jacob, for he has pursued me twice: the first time he took my birthright; and now he has taken my blessing.' Then he said: 'Have you not reserved a blessing for me?'
translations.37: And he answered, and said: 'Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given him as servants; and with grain and grape-juice I have supported him. And for you now — what shall I do, my son?'
translations.38: And Esau said to his father: 'Is it one blessing only that is yours, O my father? Bless me — me also, O my father!' And he lifted up his voice, and wept.
translations.39: And Isaac his father answered, and said to him: 'Behold — of the fat of the earth shall be your dwelling, and of the dew of the sky from above.
translations.40: And by your sword shall you live, and your brother shall you serve; and when you grow strong, you shall break his bond from upon your neck.'
translations.41: And Esau harbored hatred against Jacob, on account of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. And Esau said in himself: 'The days of mourning for my father shall draw near, and I shall kill Jacob my brother.'
translations.42: And Rebekah was told the words of Esau her elder son; and she sent, and called for Jacob her younger son, and said to him: 'Behold, Esau your brother is threatening to kill you.
translations.43: Now, my son, accept from me — arise and flee to Laban my brother, to Haran.
translations.44: And dwell with him a few days, until the wrath of your brother turns away,
translations.45: until your brother's anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him; then I shall send and take you from there. Why should I lose the two of you in one day?'
translations.46: And Rebekah said to Isaac: 'I have grown weary in my life on account of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of Heth — or from the daughters of the dwellers of the land — what is life to me?'
